messages:
eva: heads up — onboarding hit a thorny one. our sampleapp kept auth'ing with the old PROJECT key even after the ops sidecar injected an ORG key into the pod env. long-lived streams stayed on the old principal. anyone seen sdks ignore env rotations?
tom: ouch. which sdk/version and how are you rotating the env?
eva: go-sdk v1.2.5. repro: container or init writes ~/.redwood/credentials with REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT=proj-old; later the sidecar sets REDWOOD_API_KEY_ORG=org-new; but outgoing requests still show proj-old.
meera: that matches a known precedence issue — some older sdks read a credentials file (~/.redwood/credentials) and prefer it over env vars. if the file exists the client won't pick up later env updates.
tom: that explains streams reconnecting with the stale identity. quick mitigation: remove ~/.redwood/credentials in the image or startup script when env keys are present, or restart processes after rotation.
eva: we patched our init to rm the file for now. but this is a surprising onboarding gotcha. docs should call this out.
meera: UX choices: (1) prefer env always (breaking for some users), (2) emit a one-line warning when file != env, (3) provide explicit cache-invalidate API or SIGHUP handler. For 1.x warn+docs, for 2.x flip precedence.
tom: can you open an issue with a short compatibility plan? I'll coordinate sampleapp e2e that asserts identity flips on env rotation.
eva: filed DEVEX-6120: "Credential precedence & env rotation: cached file vs injected env" — attached minimal repro and logs. tagging @eng-runtime.
ops-bot: Created issue DEVEX-6120 and linked repos redwood/sdk and sampleapp.
meera: i'll draft a tiny warning PR for 1.x (log when env key present and cached file differs) and add a note in the quickstart: "If you rely on injected env rotation, ensure no cached credentials are present in the container filesystem or restart the process after rotation."
tom: assigning: @meera for SDK warning PR + unit test, @tom for sampleapp e2e, @eva for quickstart doc update.
eva: thanks — saved us a late-night pager. :relieved:
